title: VPC + KMS onboarding stepper — prototype notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc for the VPC + KMS onboarding stepper in the Private Deploy Admin Console. Intent: capture UX decisions, edge cases, acceptance criteria, and an initial groomed backlog for the engineering sprint. Focus areas: VPC setup, region selection/routing, networking validation (CIDR/subnets/peering), KMS vs HSM choices and CMK import/creation flows, required IAM roles, and audit logging visibility.

Summary of proposed UX pattern:
- Single unified stepper (left rail) for first-time private deployment: 1) Basics (name, region), 2) Network (VPC, subnets, peering), 3) Security (KMS/HSM, keys, roles), 4) Storage & Logging (S3 buckets, audit exports), 5) Review & Provision. Each step allows saving a draft and returning.
- Inline validation with non-blocking warnings: e.g., overlapping CIDR warns but allows continue with checkbox to confirm advanced network setup.
- Presets for common infra: "AWS VPC quickstart", "GCP VPC peering pattern", "Bring-your-own-VPC (advanced)". Quickstart collapses advanced fields.

Wireframe notes (visual mapping for mocks):
- Step header: step number + short tooltip icon (hover explains "why we need this").
- Right-hand flyout: contextual help + link to Confluence quickstart snippets (copy CLI commands).
- Network step: visual mini-diagram (VPC, subnets, route table icons). Clicking subnet opens modal to edit CIDR and AZ preference.
- KMS step: two large cards: 1) Redwood-managed CMK (recommended) with pros/cons, 2) Customer-managed key (BYOK) with two sub-options: imported key material OR external HSM (CloudHSM/CloudKMS with HSM). Each card lists compliance implications.

Detailed UX decisions / edge cases:
- Region pairing: allow users to choose control-plane region (where console coordinates) and inference region(s). Default inference region = control-plane region, with ability to add additional inference regions. Display latency/cost heuristic (rough).
- VPC selection: show list of detected VPCs (via customer API token & limited IAM role). If none found, show wizard for creating a minimal VPC (recommended) with sample terraform snippet.
- CIDR suggestions: suggest non-overlapping private ranges, auto-suggest /20 or /16 depending on scale. Provide "test overlap" button to run against other connected networks (requires extra permission).
- Peering vs Transit: distinguish peering for single VPC <-> Redwood vs Transit Gateway for multiple VPCs. For Transit Gateway show additional note: "will require route propagation setup; we cannot modify customer's route tables — operator action required".
- Security group / firewall: allow optional template to create per-subnet SGs with minimal ports (9000, 443, 22 optional). Emphasize least privilege.
- HSM flow: for HSM-backed keys, we need two factor check: (1) KMS cluster identifier, (2) attestation proof or customer KMS ARN. Show checklist: customer has HSM, HSM accessible from inference VPC via peering, KMS policy includes Redwood service principal.

KMS-specific UX and acceptance criteria:
- Option A: Redwood-managed key (default)
  - Pros: simple, quicker provisioning, Redwood rotates and backs key.
  - Acceptance: one-click enable, console shows key ID and region; auditing shows RW actions.
- Option B: Customer-managed key (BYOK) - import key material
  - Console asks for key alias, ARN, and optionally upload of key wrapping certificate.
  - Acceptance: console validates ARN and that key policy grants Redwood encryption/decryption. If validation fails, show clear troubleshooting suggestions and sample IAM policy snippet.
- Option C: Customer HSM / external KMS integration
  - Provide checklist + preflight test: verify network connectivity, KMS policy, and attestation tokens (if required).
  - Acceptance: preflight succeeds; UI shows green checks for connectivity, key policy, and attestation.

Backlog grooming (candidate stories, priority, size) — rough notes: (use PD-#### ids as placeholders)
- PD-1101: Stepper scaffold + step headers + save-as-draft (P0, 3)
- PD-1102: Region selector + multi-region tag UI (P0, 2)
- PD-1103: VPC discovery API integration + minimal VPC wizard (P0, 5)
- PD-1104: CIDR validation + overlap tester (P1, 3)
- PD-1105: KMS card designs + Redwood-managed key flow (P0, 3)
- PD-1106: BYOK import flow + policy validation (P1, 5)
- PD-1107: HSM preflight checks + attestation UX (P1, 8)
- PD-1108: Networking diagram mini-canvas + subnet editor modal (P2, 5)
- PD-1109: Audit log visibility panel (P1, 2)
- PD-1110: CLI/terraform snippets generation for each config (P2, 3)

Open questions (need answers before dev):
- Should Redwood be able to create route table entries in customer accounts? (Security team leaning: no — require operator action).
- For VPC discovery, what minimally scoped IAM role do we request? Need a security review on the exact permissions.
- For BYOK imports, do we accept raw key material via UI or only KMS import APIs? (Ops: importing raw material triggers compliance workflow).
- What telemetry can we send to helpdesk during preflight without leaking key identifiers? (privacy + security check).

Accessibility + copy notes:
- Error messages must be actionable (not just "validation failed"). Provide explicit commands or policy snippets to paste into IAM console.
- Use progressive disclosure for advanced fields and show inline "Why would I choose this?" tooltips.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- User can complete the stepper end-to-end and land on a review page with a full JSON config preview that can be handed to infra or applied by CLI.
- Preflight connectivity checks for KMS/HSM and VPC peering return deterministic PASS/WARN/FAIL with logs available in the audit panel.
- BYOK flow validates key policy and surfaces minimum remediation steps.
- Drafts persist reliably and are re-openable by other users in the same org (collab).

Implementation notes for eng (ops/infra handoff):
- Preflight runner should be an asynchronous job (status polled) because network checks may take minutes. Provide webhook/notify option for completion.
- Keep all key metadata out of logs (only show hashed IDs) to avoid PII/KMS leak.
- Expose a read-only JSON representation of the final configuration and a generated terraform snippet to help customers with IaC.

Next steps / short-term owner list:
- Aisha: consolidate IAM permissions list for VPC discovery + share with Security (due 2026-03-17).
- Marco: prototype mini-canvas for subnet editor (due 2026-03-24).
- Evelyn: mock the KMS cards + copy (due 2026-03-20).
- Tomás: draft preflight API contract (due 2026-03-22).

Notes to self / friction log (raw):
- Need to minimize number of permissions asked at first-run — UX dropoff if we ask for too many IAM scopes.
- Customers often confuse "control plane region" vs "inference region". Call them out with example use-cases.
- HSM customers will demand attestation logs and possibly an offline signing flow — flag this to legal for contract implications.

END — save as draft and share with design + security.

Reference sketches attached (in GH PR / mock folder): see linked_artifacts.
